discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France and Flatiron Institute

motivation: Vollhardt, with Metzner, showed that the limit of infinite spatial dimensions gives a nontrivial, exactly solvable limit of the Hubbard model. Georges and Kotliar then showed that in this limit the lattice problem maps exactly onto a quantum impurity embedded in a self-consistent bath. The result, dynamical mean-field theory, gave the first controlled, nonperturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It explained the coexistence of quasiparticles and Hubbard bands seen in photoemission and optics. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became a quantitative, predictive framework for real correlated materials, including transition-metal oxides, actinides, iron pnictides and nickelates. Its cluster and nonequilibrium extensions now underpin a large share of modern quantum-materials research. Few theoretical ideas have so thoroughly changed how physicists understand and compute the behaviour of interacting electrons in solids.
